question: Can the synthetic richness/composition hierarchy be confronted with a real transition-linked Izu chain measured on the same tagged plants within prespecified field blocks?

block_definition.rule: A block is a prespecified population/site/time window within which visitor exposure, single-visit deposition assays, and reproductive-treatment assignment are linked before reproductive outcomes are known.

starting_state: pre-outcome floral geometry measured on the same plant
community_exposure: usable observation effort including zero-visit windows
visitor identity/group on the same block
effectiveness: single-visit pollen deposition on a previously unvisited receptive stigma
rate-weighted effective pollen delivery where controlled
seed_outcome: mature fruit linkage through fruit_id when applicable
mature seed count for every mature linked fruit

synthetic_to_empirical_mapping.synthetic_realized_richness: block-level observed visitor richness, reported with observation effort and zero-visit windows; controlled-effective visitor-group count is a second richness-like exposure measure
synthetic_to_empirical_mapping.synthetic_realized_composition: block-level visitor-group composition and controlled effective-service composition based on visit rate x background-adjusted SVD
synthetic_to_empirical_mapping.synthetic_starting_state: same-plant pre-outcome floral geometry / corrected functional position; no phenotype measured after the response may be back-filled as starting state
synthetic_to_empirical_mapping.synthetic_branch_identity: same-plant downstream response conditional on block exposure, represented by dependency and mature-seed outcomes rather than a synthetic sign label

primary_hierarchy.coarse_regime_test: Ask whether block richness-like exposure predicts the block/plant mean level of effective service and downstream reproductive response.
primary_hierarchy.branch_test: After accounting for richness-like exposure, ask whether realized effective-service composition interacts with plant starting state to explain residual plant-level dependency/seed response.
primary_hierarchy.transition_chain_test: Visitor exposure -> visitor-specific SVD/effective service -> reproductive dependency/pollen limitation -> mature seed, all within the same block and tagged plant panel.

full_chain_plant: plant is registered in the block population/site
at least one usable observation-effort row in the block
at least one linked single-visit SVD row and at least one no-visit SVD control on that plant in the block
all three core reproductive treatments are assigned on that plant in the block
all core treatments have terminal analyzable outcomes; every mature_fruit outcome links to a fruit row with mature_seed_count
pre-outcome floral geometry exists for the same plant
structural_admission.full_chain_block: At least one full-chain plant exists. This is structural completion only and is not a precision/power claim.
structural_admission.confirmatory_adequacy: Remains closed until pilot dispersion, independent-plant replication, repeated temporal/site blocks, and precision goals pass the existing planning gates.

decision_states.protocol_ready: schemas and audit can encode the chain
decision_states.field_chain_observed: at least one full-chain block passes structural admission
decision_states.hierarchy_estimable: enough independent plants/blocks exist to fit richness and composition x starting-state terms without post-hoc simplification
decision_states.transition_linked_support: the visitor -> SVD/service -> dependency -> seed chain is supported in the prespecified model with uncertainty
decision_states.historical_causal_transition: not opened by this design alone

claim_boundary: This design can convert the synthetic richness/composition hierarchy into a directly measured contemporary Izu transition-linked chain. It does not by itself identify historical Bombus loss, evolutionary selection, a universal island syndrome, or natural prevalence of synthetic response branches.
